title: Kth Largest Element in a Stream
hints: re-sorting everything after every single new value is wasteful - most of the collection doesn't change
you only ever need the k largest values; anything smaller than those can be discarded permanently
keep a min-heap holding exactly the k largest values seen so far; its smallest element (the top) is the kth largest

seed the heap with the initial list, trimming down to size k. for each new stream value, push it, and if the heap now has more than k elements, pop the smallest; the top of the heap after each step is your answer
commonMistakes: rebuilding the heap from scratch on every new arrival instead of maintaining it incrementally
using a max-heap of everything and popping k times per query, which is far slower than a bounded min-heap
forgetting to trim the initial list down to size k before processing the first stream value

content.problemStatement:
You start with an initial list of numbers and a fixed value `k`. Then,
one at a time, new numbers arrive and get added to the collection.
After each new number is added, you need to know the `k`th largest
value in the collection so far (counting from the largest, with
duplicates counted separately).

**Return an array holding the `k`th largest value after each addition,
in the order the numbers arrived.**

The collection is guaranteed to always have at least `k` elements
whenever a result is requested.
constraints: the collection always has at least k elements whenever a kth-largest value is needed
notes: empty stream, meaning no results should be returned
k equal to the size of the initial list
stream values smaller than every existing element, not changing the answer

sampleTestCases.explanation: starting from [4,5,8,2], the 3rd largest is 4; after adding 3 it's still 4; after adding 5 the collection has two 5s so the 3rd largest becomes 5; after adding 10 the top three are 10,8,5 so it's 5; after adding 9 the top three are 10,9,8 so it's 8; after adding 4 the top three are still 10,9,8 so it's 8
the 1st largest (the maximum) stays 3 throughout since every value is 3
no values arrive from the stream, so no results are produced

optimal.time: O((n + m) log k) for n initial values and m stream values
optimal.pattern: a min-heap of size k, maintained incrementally as new values arrive

bruteForce.approach: after each new value arrives, sort all elements seen so far descending and read off index k - 1
bruteForce.time: O(n^2 log n) across all additions
